ORCA HMD – Operator Robotic Control Apparatus

Operator Robotic Control Apparatus · head-mounted display (HMD) recon sim, first playableORCA HMD build 5 · VR buttons

The light is going. Walk to overwatch, use two drones to see ahead, change sensors as it gets dark, and mark every hostile in the village before they see you. Hidden bombs (IEDs) lie on the roads and trails. Then walk out.

Everything you do is recorded from the moment this page opens: where you walk and look, who could see whom, sensor changes, orders, messages, keys and buttons. At the end of the mission you get a report. The record is kept in this browser and, when you are online, saved to the page’s store too. Settings can switch off the online copy.

IED means improvised explosive device, a hidden bomb. It lies on roads and trails and goes off if you pass within 2 metres. Sensors and drones reveal it.

On the briefing table you can plan a route for each ground robot: pick the BLR, the robot dog or the Rover, then click the map to drop waypoints. When you deploy, each robot drives its route, then holds. A waypoint on a tunnel entrance sends the robot down to search the tunnel. The plan is kept for next time.

The Rover 8×8 carries five launcher boxes, each with a small scout drone. Press T until you look through the rover, then L to launch one, J to launch all, K to recall them. It must be stopped to launch.

Platform: TerminaThor, Unmanned Operating System of the Fuse Urban Lethality System. Drones: MagniTude and Magni-X.

Past the village the main road runs east into a bigger town, with a market and a walled hostile base at its far corner. A tunnel runs from the base, under the town, to an entrance just north of the market. Robots go first: point at an entrance, or plan it on the table, to send the robot dog or the BLR down to search it. Once a robot has searched it, you can walk down too. Settings can change this rule. Drones cannot see underground.

You have a body. You do not see it, only your hands and weapon, but every drone and robot sees it, with a green YOU mark: a ring, an arrow for the way you face, a wedge for what your eyes cover, and your compass heading. Settings can switch the mark off.

The rear view strip appears under the heading tape by itself when a hostile is behind you, shown like a mirror. Press V, the Rear button, or the left thumbstick to keep it on. Settings can flip it or turn it off.

Characters: Microsoft Rocketbox avatar library, MIT licence. Hands: built on the WebXR Input Profiles generic hand model, W3C Software and Document License.

Hand signalHow, with hand tracking in a headsetWhat the robots do
HaltClosed fist raised beside your head, held stillStop and hold
Rally on meIndex finger up above your head, circledCome to you
PointOnly the index finger out, arm out, held stillNearest ground robot goes there. Pointing at a robot picks it for your next signal
AdvanceOpen hand swung from above your head forward and down, palm downBack to its own job
ForwardFist, palm down, pushed straight out from your chestGround robots move 10 m the way you face
BackFist, palm down, pulled in toward your chestGround robots move 10 m back toward you

Signals come from your left hand, so your right stays on the weapon. Each robot that takes a signal answers with a double chirp. Without hand tracking, press H or the Signal button and pick a signal. Point then uses the centre of your view.

On a phone: drag the left side of the screen to walk and the right side to look. To mark, tap the person, or aim and press Mark. Landscape works best.
